title: Envisioning the near future of technology
author: Michell Zappa (Envisioning Technology)
frame: Radial chart. Distance from 'now (2011)' places each technology in one of three bands: 2011-2015, 2015-2025, 2025+. Band placements are graded against the band end year (placed_year). Nodes that sit on a ring are read as that ring's year.

entries.label: Print on demand
entries.claim: Print on demand becomes mainstream within 2011–2015
entries.interpretation: Under MATERIALS: physical goods (books, merchandise, 3D-printed parts) printed or made on demand instead of mass-produced for stock.
entries.verdict_reason: Book print-on-demand was already mainstream before the band: Bowker counted non-traditional, mostly POD titles above traditional titles from 2008, and nearly 8 times as many in 2010, 7 years before the 2015 band end. On-demand manufacturing of objects (Shapeways-style 3D printing services) stayed niche through 2015. Under the MATERIALS reading, real but niche adoption by 2015 gives partial; the book reading gives an early forecast of 5+ years, also no better than partial.

evidence.title: Print Isn't Dead, Says Bowker's Annual Book Production Report
evidence.shows: Non-traditional (largely print-on-demand) US titles rose to about 2.8 million in 2010, far above traditional output.

evidence.title: Non-Traditional Books Lead Industry's Growth
evidence.shows: POD book output overtook traditional publishing by 2008-2009.

entries.label: Memristor
entries.interpretation: Memristor devices in mass-produced memory or computing products by 2015.
entries.verdict_reason: Industrial/consumer test. HP planned memristor memory with Hynix for 2013 but dropped it from The Machine in 2015 and used DRAM instead. Resistive RAM exists only in niche embedded memory. Memristors were not mainstream by 2020 (band end + 5) or today, so this is a miss.

evidence.title: HP Puts the Future of Computing On Hold | MIT Technology Review
evidence.shows: HP postponed memristor-based computing in 2015, the band end year.

evidence.title: HP Removes Memristors from Its 'Machine' Roadmap Until Further Notice - HPCwire
evidence.shows: The main commercial memristor program was shelved indefinitely.

entries.label: Cermets
entries.interpretation: Ceramic-metal composite materials (cermets) in widespread industrial use, e.g. cutting tools, wear parts, solar absorber coatings.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: industrial standard practice. Cermet cutting tools were introduced in the 1950s and Sumitomo launched TiC-based cermet inserts in 1960; cermets were an established tooling class decades before the 2011-2015 band. The early rule puts mainstream arrival more than 5 years before the placed year in miss: the forecast was late by about 50 years. It is not unfalsifiable because the label names a clear material class.

evidence.title: Brands History Chapter 2-2, Sumitomo Electric Hardmetal
evidence.shows: Sumitomo released its TiC-based cermet line TICUT in 1960.

evidence.title: The Time is Right for Cermets (Cutting Tool Engineering)
evidence.shows: Cermet cutting tools date to the 1950s and are a mature tooling class.

entries.label: Bio-enhanced fuels
entries.note: Band 2011–2015 (r≈249 pt). Close to a band edge (6 pt); the node overlaps the ring.

entries.label: Ultra-capacitors
entries.interpretation: Ultracapacitors (supercapacitors) as a common energy-storage component in vehicles, grid and consumer devices.
entries.verdict_reason: Energy test. Ultracapacitors had real commercial uses by 2015 (hybrid buses, rail, wind-turbine pitch control, some automotive start-stop), but the market was small: leader Maxwell's ultracapacitor revenue fell to $114.5 million in 2015. They took no material share of energy storage, which lithium-ion batteries dominated. Real niche adoption at the band end gives partial; not a miss because commercial deployment existed.

evidence.title: Maxwell Technologies Inc Form 10-K FY2015
evidence.shows: Maxwell ultracapacitor revenue fell 16% to $114.5 million in 2015, with sales in transit, wind and automotive niches.

entries.label: Gamification of media
entries.claim: Gamification of media becomes mainstream within 2011–2015
entries.interpretation: Game mechanics (points, badges, leaderboards, streaks) built into media consumption such as news, TV and publishing.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: abstract practice routinely occurring. Gamification peaked as a trend in 2011-2013 and spread in apps (Foursquare, Duolingo streaks, social TV check-ins), but in media proper it stayed a set of experiments; Gartner predicted in 2012 that 80% of gamified applications would fail by 2014, and many media badge programmes closed. Real but niche adoption within the band, so partial. Not a hit because gamified news or TV consumption never became normal practice.

evidence.title: Badges Beware: 80% Of Gamification Apps Will End Up Being Losers, Says Gartner
evidence.shows: Gartner expected most gamified applications to fail their objectives by 2014.

evidence.title: Gartner Study: Gamification Not Built to Last
evidence.shows: Contemporary analysis saw gamification as a fad-prone practice, not a settled norm.

entries.label: All media on demand
entries.claim: All media on demand becomes mainstream within 2011–2015
entries.interpretation: Video, music and other media consumed on demand by streaming instead of scheduled broadcast or owned copies.
entries.verdict_reason: By 2015, 52% of US households had Netflix, Amazon Prime or Hulu, and digital overtook physical in global recorded music revenue with streaming growing 45%. That meets the consumer test (well over 10% of households) inside the 2011-2015 band. 'All' media was not fully on demand (live TV persisted), but the dominant formats were.

evidence.title: Netflix, Amazon or Hulu SVOD in 74% of U.S. Households
evidence.shows: Leichtman data: 52% of US households had a major SVOD service in 2015.

evidence.title: IFPI Global Report: Digital Revenues Surpass Physical for the First Time as Streaming Explodes
evidence.shows: In 2015 digital music revenue passed physical and streaming grew 45%.

entries.label: Holography
entries.note: Node centre sits on the ring between the 2011–2015 and 2015–2025 bands (r≈254 pt, ring at ≈255 pt); read as 2015.

entries.label: Electronic paper
entries.note: Node centre sits on the ring between the 2011–2015 and 2015–2025 bands (r≈254 pt, ring at ≈255 pt); read as 2015.
entries.interpretation: Electronic-paper (e-ink) displays in widely owned consumer devices such as e-readers.
entries.verdict_reason: Consumer test. Pew measured US adult e-reader ownership at 24% in September 2013 and 32% in January 2014, and e-ink shelf labels spread in retail. Mainstream by 2013-2014 is within 2 years of 2015, so this is a hit. It is not early by more than 2 years, because ownership was still below about 12% in 2011.

evidence.title: E-Reading Rises as Device Ownership Jumps | Pew Research Center
evidence.shows: 32% of US adults owned an e-reader in January 2014.

evidence.title: The rise of e-reading | Pew Research Center
evidence.shows: E-reader ownership was growing from a low base in 2011-2012.

entries.label: PAN
entries.interpretation: Personal Area Networks: short-range wireless links between a person's devices (Bluetooth / IEEE 802.15, including Bluetooth LE wearables).
entries.verdict_reason: Test: infrastructure used by a large share of users. Bluetooth PAN was already mainstream before the band: the one-billionth Bluetooth device shipped in November 2006 at 12 million per week. PAN was mainstream during 2011-2015, but it arrived about 4-5 years before the band opened, so the forecast was late; partial under the early rule. If the poster meant BLE wearable networks specifically, 2013-2015 wearables would make it a hit.

evidence.title: Over One Billion Bluetooth Products Shipped
evidence.shows: Bluetooth PAN reached one billion devices in 2006, years before the 2011-2015 band.

entries.label: Social graph
entries.interpretation: The mapped network of personal connections (Facebook-style social graph) as a core layer of the web, used for identity, login and sharing.
entries.verdict_reason: Consumer test. Social networking use among US adults rose to 65% by 2015, and Facebook's social graph powered login and sharing across the web through Facebook Connect and Open Graph. The social graph was mainstream inside the 2011 to 2015 band. Hit by the band rule.

evidence.title: Social Media Usage: 2005-2015
evidence.shows: 65% of US adults used social networking sites in 2015, up from 7% in 2005.

entries.label: Semantic web
entries.interpretation: Machine-readable semantic data embedded in web pages and used by major services (schema.org markup, knowledge graphs), the practical form of the W3C Semantic Web.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: infrastructure widely deployed. Schema.org launched in 2011; by 2015, 31.3% of pages in a 10-billion-page sample carried schema.org markup, and Google, Bing and Yahoo consumed it for rich results and knowledge graphs. Mainstream by the band end 2015, so hit. The strict W3C vision (RDF/OWL reasoning by software agents across the web) stayed niche; under that reading the verdict is partial.

evidence.title: Schema.org: Evolution of Structured Data on the Web
evidence.shows: 31.3% of sampled pages had schema.org markup in 2015, up from 22% a year earlier; at least 12 million sites used it.

entries.label: Linked data
entries.interpretation: Structured, machine-readable data linked across the web with shared vocabularies (RDF, schema.org, knowledge graphs).
entries.verdict_reason: Schema.org launched in 2011, Google's Knowledge Graph in 2012 and Wikidata in 2012. By 2015, 31.3% of sampled web pages carried schema.org markup, up from 22% a year earlier, and search engines used it routinely. That meets the infrastructure test (widely deployed and used) inside the 2011-2015 band, though as pragmatic structured data rather than the full Semantic Web vision.

evidence.title: Schema.org: Evolution of Structured Data on the Web (CACM)
evidence.shows: 31.3% of pages in a 10-billion-page sample had schema.org markup in 2015.

evidence.title: Four years of Schema.org - Recent Progress and Looking Forward
evidence.shows: Google reported broad schema.org adoption by 2015.

entries.label: Medical diagnostics
entries.interpretation: AI software that performs or assists medical diagnosis as standard clinical practice.
entries.verdict_reason: Medical test. The FDA list held about 1,250 AI-enabled devices by end-2025, over three quarters in radiology. An ESR survey found 48% of European radiologists using AI clinically in 2024, up from 20% in 2018. Approved, widely used diagnostic AI inside the 2015-2025 band makes this a hit. Reimbursement stays limited and adoption outside radiology is thin, which is the main argument for partial.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices - FDA
evidence.shows: FDA lists over a thousand authorized AI-enabled medical devices, mostly diagnostic imaging.

evidence.title: Impact of AI on radiology: a EuroAIM/EuSoMII 2024 survey among members of the European Society of Radiology
evidence.shows: 48% of surveyed European radiologists used AI in clinical practice in 2024.

entries.label: Natural language interpretation
entries.claim: Natural language interpretation becomes mainstream around 2025

entries.label: VASIMR
entries.note: Node centre sits on the ring between the 2015–2025 and 2025+ bands (r≈431 pt, ring at ≈431 pt); read as 2025.
entries.interpretation: The VASIMR plasma engine in routine operational use for spacecraft propulsion.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: industrial standard practice (flight use). VASIMR has never flown. Its best result is an 88-hour, 80 kW ground endurance test in July 2021 under NASA NextSTEP, aiming at TRL 5. Nothing shows a flight unit being built, so mainstream use by 2030 is very unlikely. Miss, provisional until the window closes in 2030.

evidence.title: VASIMR VX-200SS Plasma Rocket Completes Record 88-Hour High Power Endurance Test
evidence.shows: VASIMR remained a ground test article in 2021.

evidence.title: Steady-State Testing in the VASIMR VX-200SS Project
evidence.shows: The program goal is a TRL 5 ground demonstration, not a flight engine.

entries.label: Multi-segmented smart grids
entries.claim: Multi-segmented smart grids becomes mainstream around 2025

entries.label: Superconducting interties
entries.interpretation: Superconducting links that tie separate power grids together (interties), for example the Tres Amigas hub.
entries.verdict_reason: Infrastructure test. The flagship superconducting intertie, Tres Amigas, lost its Eastern link in 2015 and went silent after 2017. Superconducting cables that do run in grids (LIPA 2008, AmpaCity Essen, Shanghai 2021, Munich SuperLink in testing in 2024 to 2025) are short distribution or urban links, not interties. No superconducting intertie is in commercial service by 2025. Miss, and the intertie form was abandoned.

evidence.title: Tres Amigas developer: SPS pullout of deal 'not that significant'
evidence.shows: The main superconducting intertie project lost its Eastern Interconnection partner in 2015.

evidence.title: Superconducting high-power cables and lines—development status and technology roadmap
evidence.shows: Superconducting cables operate in a small number of distribution-grid projects, and the field is still at roadmap stage.

entries.label: Nanostructure battery cathodes
entries.claim: Nanostructure battery cathodes becomes mainstream within 2015–2025
entries.interpretation: Nanostructured cathode materials (e.g. nanoscale, carbon-coated LiFePO4 particles) in mass-market lithium-ion batteries.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: energy, material share of the market. LFP cathodes, which depend on nanoscale carbon-coated particles to overcome low conductivity, reached almost half of the global EV battery market by 2024 per the IEA. Mainstream inside the 2015-2025 band. Hit. Caveat: commercial LFP uses sub-micron primary particles and nanocoatings rather than exotic nanostructures such as nanowires, which stayed in the lab.

evidence.title: Electric vehicle batteries - Global EV Outlook 2025
evidence.shows: LFP accounted for almost half of the global EV battery market in 2024.

evidence.title: Recent Development in Carbon-LiFePO4 Cathodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries: A Mini Review
evidence.shows: Nano-sized, carbon-coated LiFePO4 particles are the standard route to usable LFP performance.

entries.label: PV at grid parity
entries.claim: PV at grid parity becomes mainstream within 2015–2025
entries.interpretation: Solar PV electricity at or below the cost of conventional grid power, and deployed at scale on that basis.
entries.verdict_reason: In 2016 solar PV added over 74 GW and grew faster than any other fuel, with auction prices near 3 US cents/kWh. IRENA found utility PV costs fell 85% from 2010 to 2020 and most new renewables undercut the cheapest new fossil option by 2020. PV became a material share of new capacity at grid parity inside the 2015-2025 band (energy test).

evidence.title: Solar PV grew faster than any other fuel in 2016, opening a new era for solar power
evidence.shows: Solar PV added over 74 GW in 2016 and led net capacity growth, with record-low auction prices.

evidence.title: Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2020
evidence.shows: Utility PV cost fell 85% in 2010-2020 and was cheaper than new fossil capacity in most markets.

entries.label: Solar thermal
entries.note: Band 2015–2025 (r≈424 pt). Close to a band edge (7 pt); the node overlaps the ring.
entries.interpretation: Solar thermal power (concentrated solar power) as a material share of new generating capacity.
entries.verdict_reason: Energy test. Global CSP capacity reached only about 6.9 GW by 2024, against about 1,865 GW of solar PV; CSP is a negligible share of new capacity. PV displaced it. Solar water heating is a separate case: it was already mainstream in China before 2011 and its market has shrunk since 2013, so that reading is also a miss (early). Either reading gives miss. Provisional: the 5-year window closes in 2030.

evidence.title: Renewable power generation costs in 2024 - IRENA
evidence.shows: CSP capacity stayed around 7 GW while solar PV passed 1,800 GW.

evidence.title: Solar Heat Worldwide 2025 - IEA SHC
evidence.shows: Solar thermal collector installations have fallen by more than half since 2013.

entries.label: Location-aware media
entries.interpretation: Media and content that adapt to or are tagged with the user's location (geotagged posts and photos, location-based recommendations, maps and check-ins).
entries.verdict_reason: Test: consumer product at 10%+ of people. Pew found 74% of US smartphone owners used location-based services in early 2012, when about 46% of adults owned smartphones, so roughly a third of adults already used location-aware content in 2012. It was mainstream through the band, but it arrived about 3 years before the 2015-2025 band opened; the forecast was late, which the early rule grades partial. A hit would need mainstream arrival within the band.

evidence.title: Three-quarters of smartphone owners use location-based services
evidence.shows: 74% of smartphone owners used location-based information in 2012.

evidence.title: Location-Based Services (Pew Research Center)
evidence.shows: Location-based services were mass use among smartphone owners by 2013.

entries.label: Immersive 3D projections
entries.interpretation: Projected three-dimensional imagery that surrounds or floats in front of users without headsets (holographic and room-scale immersive projection) as an everyday natural interface.
entries.verdict_reason: Consumer test. By 2025 real niche forms existed: immersive projection venues such as Sphere Las Vegas (opened 2023), immersive art exhibitions, and holographic displays such as Looking Glass monitors. The holographic display market was only about $4.3 billion in 2025 and served B2B, retail and entertainment niches. It never became a common interface in homes or offices within the 2015 to 2025 band. Partial for real niche adoption; the label is loose, which is a second reason not to go further.

evidence.title: Holographic Display Market Size, Growth Outlook 2025-2034
evidence.shows: Holographic and glasses-free 3D displays remained a small market focused on niche B2B uses in 2025.

evidence.title: The Future Of Immersive Entertainment Is Now - The Sphere Experience Premieres Tomorrow
evidence.shows: Large immersive projection experiences exist as single flagship venues, not as a common interface.

entries.label: Fabric-embedded screens
entries.note: Node centre sits on the ring between the 2015–2025 and 2025+ bands (r≈429 pt, ring at ≈431 pt); read as 2025.

entries.label: SPIMES
entries.interpretation: SPIMES: everyday objects with identities that are tracked through space and time over their lifecycle (item-level RFID, Bluetooth trackers, connected product records).
entries.verdict_reason: Test: consumer and industrial practice widely deployed. By the early 2020s about 47% of items received by apparel and general-merchandise retailers carried RFID tags, and Apple sold an estimated 55 million AirTags in 2021-2022 on a crowd-sourced tracking network. Item-level tracking became routine inside the 2015-2025 band, so hit. Sterling's full vision (cradle-to-grave data for every object, recycling included) is not there yet; EU digital product passports start after 2025.

evidence.title: Survey says nearly half of product manufacturers implementing item-level RFID
evidence.shows: Auburn RFID Lab survey: on average 47% of items received by apparel and general-merchandise retailers carry RFID tags.

evidence.title: Apple estimated to sell 55 million AirTag item trackers in first 2 years
evidence.shows: Consumer object trackers reached tens of millions of units by 2022.

entries.label: Virtual property
entries.interpretation: People buying, owning and trading virtual goods (in-game items, skins, digital assets) as property.
entries.verdict_reason: Within the 2015-2025 band, in-game item purchases became the main revenue of the games industry: all top-ten grossing digital games of 2019 were free-to-play, Fortnite cosmetics earned billions in 2018, and Newzoo put in-game purchases at about three-quarters of 2020 games revenue. Hundreds of millions of players owned virtual items, which meets the consumer test. Legal ownership stays platform-controlled and NFT-based ownership collapsed, but the label's ownership of virtual goods is mainstream.

evidence.title: Newzoo Predicts $200 Billion Gaming Market By 2023, 77% Of It From In-Game Purchases
evidence.shows: Newzoo estimated most games revenue came from in-game purchases of virtual items.

evidence.title: Epic Games, the creator of Fortnite, banked a $3 billion profit in 2018
evidence.shows: Fortnite's cosmetic item sales produced billions in 2018.

entries.label: Sensors
entries.interpretation: Networked sensors as a node under connectivity, roughly the sensor side of the Internet of Things.
entries.verdict_reason: A bare 'Sensors' label names a component class, not a product or practice. Sensors were already ubiquitous and networked in 2011 (smartphone GPS and accelerometers, industrial SCADA), so no adoption threshold separates before and after the 2015-2025 band. If read narrowly as IoT, connected devices reached about 18.8 billion in 2024 and it would be a hit, but the label does not fix that reading.

evidence.title: Number of connected IoT devices 2024 growing 13% to 18.8 billion globally - IoT Analytics
evidence.shows: Networked devices were ubiquitous by 2024, which fits the IoT reading, but the label does not define a threshold.

entries.label: 5G
entries.note: Band 2015–2025 (r≈422 pt). Close to a band edge (9 pt); the node overlaps the ring.

entries.label: Exoskeletons

entries.label: Tele-medicine
entries.note: Band 2015–2025 (r≈262 pt). Close to a band edge (7 pt); the node overlaps the ring.
entries.interpretation: Remote clinical consultation and care delivered over video or phone as routine, reimbursed practice.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: medical standard practice (routine, reimbursed). Medicare telehealth visits rose 63-fold from about 840,000 in 2019 to 52.7 million in 2020, and about a third of behavioral health visits moved to telehealth. Reimbursement expanded in 2020, so it became routine practice inside the 2015-2025 band.

evidence.title: New HHS study shows 63-fold increase in Medicare telehealth utilization during the pandemic
evidence.shows: Medicare telehealth visits went from 840,000 in 2019 to 52.7 million in 2020.

evidence.title: National Survey Trends in Telehealth Use in 2021 (HHS ASPE)
evidence.shows: Telehealth stayed in wide use across the US population in 2021.

entries.label: Regenerative medicine
entries.note: Node centre sits on the ring between the 2015–2025 and 2025+ bands (r≈431 pt, ring at ≈431 pt); read as 2025.
entries.interpretation: Therapies that repair or replace damaged cells, tissues or organs (stem-cell, engineered-tissue and cell/gene therapies) as standard clinical practice.
entries.verdict_reason: Medical test. By 2025 there were real approved products (36 gene therapies and 71 non-modified cell therapies worldwide), and FDA had granted 184 RMAT designations. But most are for rare diseases or cancers, with high prices and small patient numbers; pluripotent stem-cell products had dosed only about 1,200 patients in trials by end 2024. Tissue and organ regeneration is not routine practice. Real niche adoption at 2025 gives partial. Blood stem-cell transplants are routine but were routine long before 2011, so they do not make the forecast a hit.

evidence.title: Alliance for Regenerative Medicine Sector Snapshot
evidence.shows: Approved regenerative products number in the dozens worldwide, while most programs are still in clinical trials.

evidence.title: Cumulative CBER Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) Designation Requests Received by Fiscal Year
evidence.shows: FDA tracks RMAT designations for investigational regenerative therapies, most still pre-approval.
